Of course! Here's a funny observation about anime:

In any normal fight, the goal is to be unpredictable and hit your opponent when they least expect it.

In an anime fight, the
rules are:
1.  You must stand perfectly still and scream for three full episodes to power up. This is called a "training arc."
2.  You must clearly announce the full, unnecessarily long name of your attack before you use it. (e.g., "ETERNAL MIDNIGHT DRAGON VORTEX SLASH!")
3.  If you're about to lose, you must have a flashback about your friends. This "Power of Friendship" provides a bigger boost than any training you've ever done.
4.  Your opponent is legally obligated to wait for all of this to finish before they do anything.

Basically, an anime brawl is less of a fight and more of a loud, turn-based PowerPoint presentation about who has the most feelings.
